extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners studying humor and joke production (e.g., cognitive psychologists, humor scientists, comedians, comedy writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing jokes or humorous performances for presence and quality of surprise, forms of incongruity, norm-violation, benign appraisal, temporal peak, and timing scaffolding, based on Benign Violation Theory and related temporal-dynamics findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise (unexpected outcome)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the material produces an outcome that is unexpected for the audience. Note that surprise is necessary for humor but not sufficient—many surprises are not funny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Juxtaposition (two unlike things side by side)
rubrics_metrics.description: Juxtaposition — two unlike things side by side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether humor arises from placing dissimilar concepts or categories together. Juxtaposition can create incongruity but by itself does not guarantee funniness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atypicality (divergence from norm)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the content departs from typical patterns, rules, or expectations. Atypicality creates surprise/novelty; however, atypicality alone does not reliably predict humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation (threat to 'ought' beliefs)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify whether the surprise represents a violation of social, moral, linguistic, or normative expectations—i.e., something that threatens what 'ought' to be. Violations that are meaningful/important are more likely to produce humor when other conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incongruity alone insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Incongruity alone does not adequately differentiate humorous from non-humorous experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a meta-criterion: do not score humor solely on presence of incongruity. Check whether additional conditions (importance of violated norm; benign appraisal; timing) are present. Antipatterns: assuming any unexpected or atypical item is funny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benignness of violation (Benign Violation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only violations that are simultaneously benign tend to be funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the violation registers as safe, non-threatening, or otherwise acceptable to the audience. Consider factors that render a violation benign (distance, lack of real harm, contextual cues). Example anti-pattern: a morally threatening violation that is not framed as benign will be judged as offensive rather than humorous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance of violated norm (importance of violation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The surprise must violate something important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the violated expectation pertains to beliefs or norms that matter to the audience; trivial or inconsequential violations may elicit surprise but not humor. This captures the idea that meaningfulness of the violation interacts with benignness to produce humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peak violation (concentration at the punch)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peak semantic violations matter more than average incongruity levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure whether the violation is concentrated at a punchline or moment of peak surprise rather than spread evenly. Successful jokes tend to have a high, localized incongruity at the punch; average levels of incongruity across a piece are less predictive of funniness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing scaffolding (pauses before peak surprise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing scaffolds the surprise (pauses). Pauses systematically lengthen before high-surprise punchlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the performative timing: are pauses, pacing, and strategic coupling used to build expectation and amplify the punch? Check for systematic lengthening of pauses before the punch and other temporal techniques that scaffold the surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear surprise / unexpected outcome (Rubric Q1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a clear surprise / unexpected outcome?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit rubric check: confirm a distinct unexpected outcome is present. Use audience expectations as the baseline. This is the operationalized first question in the paper's summary rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of a norm (Rubric Q2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the surprise violate a norm (social, linguistic, moral)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit rubric check: identify which norm is violated and classify its domain (social, linguistic, moral). Consider the strength of the norm and its relevance to the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation simultaneously safe/benign (Rubric Q3)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit rubric check: determine whether contextual cues, psychological distance, or framing render the violation non-threatening. If not benign, the item may be offensive rather than funny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation concentrated at punch (Rubric Q4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the violation peak (concentrated at the punch)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit rubric check: verify the incongruity is localized at the punchline/peak moment rather than diffuse. Peak concentration correlates with greater humor response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing scaffold present (Rubric Q5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the timing scaffolded (pause before peak surprise)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit rubric check: observe performative timing—presence of pause(s), buildup, and strategic coupling that heighten the punch. Lack of timing scaffolding is associated with reduced effectiveness of surprise.
